children: Six Flags stock fell after a fatal accident on Monday.
A fatal accident on a Six Flags Entertainment roller coaster sent shares of the amusement-park operator on Tuesday near the lowest level of the year.

Six Flags' stock (FUN) fell 11% to $10.65 - near the 52-week low of $10.45 - after an incident at Six Flags Over Georgia on Monday afternoon left one dead and several injured, according to the Cobb County Police Department. Local news reports said a man was flung from the "Goliath" roller coaster.
Six Flags, in a statement, said it is cooperating fully with the local investigation.

"We are deeply saddened by the guest incident at our park today. Our thoughts and heartfelt condolences are with the guest's family, friends, and loved ones. We are also providing support to the guests and team members affected," the company said in a statement.
Even before this incident, Six Flags has struggled. Its stock tumbled 16% after releasing second-quarter earnings on Aug.6.
The stock has lost two-thirds of its value over the last three years, according to FactSet.
Last month, activist investor Jana Partners urged the company to explore a sale, according to the Wall Street Journal.
